Rashi on Ketubot 28a:10:1.hebrew: אבל אין נאמנין כו' - דאפוקי ממונא הוא, ובעינן עדות מעלייתא. וכתובה היינו טעמא, דרוב נשים בתולות נישאות:
Rashi on Ketubot 28a:10:1.english: However, they are not deemed credible, etc. - Because it is [a matter of] extracting money, and we require proper testimony. And [regarding] a ketubah, this is the reason [that he is deemed credible]: because most women marry as virgins.

Rashi on Ketubot 28a:10:2.hebrew: מעמד ומספד - מקום היה לו כאן להספיד מתיו כשמוליכן לבית קברות שלו, ולעשות שם מעמדות ומושבות שהיו עושין שבעה למת:
Rashi on Ketubot 28a:10:2.english: Standing and eulogy - He had a place here to eulogize his dead when bringing them to his burial ground, and to perform there [the rituals of] standing and sitting, of which they would perform seven for the dead.

Rashi on Ketubot 28a:10:3.hebrew: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא אומר נאמנים - לא גרסינן ליה במתני' אלא בברייתא, ולא אדרך מעמד ומספד קאי:
Rashi on Ketubot 28a:10:3.english: Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka says: They are deemed credible - We do not read this in the Mishnah, rather in a baraita, and it does not refer to [the cases of] a path, [a place of] standing, and a eulogy.

Rashi on Ketubot 28a:12:1.english: That he is frequently with him - And in his childhood he paid attention to his father's handwriting.

Rashi on Ketubot 28a:13:1.hebrew: קיום שטרות מדרבנן - דמדאורייתא לא בעינן קיום, דאמר ר"ל (לעיל כתובות דף יח:): עדים החתומים על השטר נעשה כמי שנחקרה עדותן בב"ד:
Rashi on Ketubot 28a:13:1.english: Ratification of documents is by rabbinic law - For by Torah law we do not require ratification, as Reish Lakish said (above, Ketubot 18b): Witnesses who are signed on a document are treated as if their testimony has been examined in court.

Rashi on Ketubot 28a:13:2.hebrew: הימנוהו רבנן בדרבנן - בדבר שהוא מדבריהם האמינו, ואין זה עוקר דבר מן התורה. הם אמרו והם אמרו: הם הצריכו קיום העדות, והם הכשירו בו את אלו:
Rashi on Ketubot 28a:13:2.english: The Sages deemed him credible in [a matter of] rabbinic law - In a matter that is from their words, they deemed him credible, and this does not uproot a matter from the Torah. They said [it], and they said [it]: they required ratification of the testimony, and they validated these [witnesses] for it.

Rashi on Ketubot 28a:14:1.hebrew: גלוי מלתא בעלמא הוא - כלומר, אין הדבר צריך עדות, אלא לפרסם שיצא הדין לאור בלא גמגום:
Rashi on Ketubot 28a:14:1.english: It is merely revealing a matter - That is to say, the matter does not require testimony, but rather [serves] to publicize [it] so that the ruling comes to light without hesitation.

Rashi on Ketubot 28a:1:1.english: And if he was a priest - Even [if] she did not remarry.

Rashi on Ketubot 28a:1:2.hebrew: לא תדור עמו במבוי - שמא יבא עליה, וכהן אסור בגרושה; אבל ישראל, כל זמן שלא ניסת, תדור בשכונתו:
Rashi on Ketubot 28a:1:2.english: She may not live with him in an alleyway - Lest he have intercourse with her, and a priest is forbidden to a divorcée; but [for] an Israelite, as long as she has not married [another man], she may live in his neighborhood.

Rashi on Ketubot 28a:4:1.hebrew: ואמר רב גרס, ומהאי קרא שמעינן לה:
Rashi on Ketubot 28a:4:1.english: [The text] reads, "And Rav said," and from this verse we learn it.

Rashi on Ketubot 28a:5:1.english: He borrowed from her - While she was married to him.

Rashi on Ketubot 28a:5:2.hebrew: בנכסי אביה - שהיו בידה נכסי מלוג, ובכהן שגירש את אשתו קא מיירי:
Rashi on Ketubot 28a:5:2.english: From her father's property - Which were nikhsei melug [usufruct property] in her possession, and [the baraita] is speaking of a priest who divorced his wife.

Rashi on Ketubot 28a:5:3.hebrew: אינה נפרעת - הימנו ע"י עצמה, שלא יקרבו בדברים:
Rashi on Ketubot 28a:5:3.english: She is not repaid - from him by herself, so that they do not draw close through conversation.

Rashi on Ketubot 28a:5:4.hebrew: באבל רבתי - מסכתא היא וקורין אותה שמחות, וזו היא משנה ראשונה שלה: הגוסס הרי הוא כחי לכל דבריו:
Rashi on Ketubot 28a:5:4.english: In Evel Rabbati - It is a tractate, and they call it Semachot, and this is its first mishnah: "One who is dying is like a living person in all respects."

Rashi on Ketubot 28a:6:1.english: A betrothed man and his betrothed - He was a priest.

Rashi on Ketubot 28a:6:2.english: And didn't Rav Nachman say: [The tanna] taught in Evel Rabbati - that [a woman divorced] from betrothal collects [payment] by herself.

Rashi on Ketubot 28a:6:3.hebrew: דגייסי בהדדי - מכירין זה את זה ברמיזות וקריצות, בלע"ז פריווי"ץ:
Rashi on Ketubot 28a:6:3.english: That they are accustomed to each other - They know each other through hints and winks; in Old French, privez [intimate].

Rashi on Ketubot 28a:8:1.hebrew: זה כתב ידו של אבא - ומקיימין השטר על פיו, אע"פ שמת אביו בעוד זה קטן:
Rashi on Ketubot 28a:8:1.english: This is my father's handwriting - And they ratify the document based on his testimony, even though his father died while he was [still] a minor.

Rashi on Ketubot 28a:9:1.hebrew: שיצאת בהינומא - והוא סימן שניסת בתולה וכתובתה מאתים, כדאמרינן בריש פירקין:
Rashi on Ketubot 28a:9:1.english: Who went out with a hinnuma - And it is a sign that she was married as a virgin and her ketubah is two hundred [dinars], as we say at the beginning of our chapter.

Rashi on Ketubot 28a:9:2.hebrew: יוצא מבית הספר - כשהיינו למידין תינוקות בבית רבן, ובכולהו מפרש טעמא בגמרא:
Rashi on Ketubot 28a:9:2.english: Leaving school - When we were studying [as] children in the teacher's house; and for all of them, the reason is explained in the Gemara.

Tosafot on Ketubot 28a:11:1.hebrew: והוא שיש גדול עמו - לא קאי אתרומה, דבתרומה סגי בא', כיון דאין מעלין מתרומה דרבנן ליוחסין; דלהכי מוקי לה בתרומה דרבנן, דבתרומה דאורייתא — כיון דסבר תנא דידן דמעלין ממנה ליוחסין, כדאמרינן לקמן — אינו נאמן אפי' יש גדול עמו. הלכך בתרומה סגי באיהו לחודיה, וכל היכא דבעינן תרי מדרבנן, סגי בהוא ואחר:
Tosafot on Ketubot 28a:11:1.english: "And [this applies] when there is an adult with him" - [This] does not refer to terumah, for regarding terumah one [witness] suffices, since we do not elevate [a person] from [eating] rabbinic terumah to [presumed priestly] lineage; for it is for this reason that [the Gemara] establishes [the Mishnah] as referring to rabbinic terumah, because regarding biblical terumah — since our Tanna holds that we do elevate from it to lineage, as we say below — he is not believed even if there is an adult with him. Therefore, regarding terumah, he alone suffices, and wherever we require two [witnesses] by rabbinic law, he and another [witness] suffice.

Tosafot on Ketubot 28a:13:1.hebrew: קיום שטרות דרבנן - תימה: כיון דמדאורייתא אפילו אין עדים שיכירו חתימת העדים השטר כשר, א"כ כל אדם שירצה יזייף ויכתוב ויחתום מה שירצה ויגבה ממנו. והכא אור"י דאיכא למימר: כגון שלוה מודה שכתבו וטוען שהוא פרוע, וקסבר האי תנא דמודה בשטר שכתבו צריך לקיימו, והאי קיום הוי ודאי מדרבנן; אי נמי כגון שנתקיים משדה אחת או משתי שדות ויוצא מתחת ידי עצמו, דאמר לעיל (כתובות דף כ.) דחיישינן שמא זייף. ומיהו בריש גיטין (דף ג. ושם) מוכח דאפילו היכא דאין מכירין החתימה כלל הוי מדאורייתא כמי שנחקרה עדותן בב"ד:
Tosafot on Ketubot 28a:13:1.english: "Ratification of documents is by rabbinic law" - This is astonishing: since by Torah law, even if there are no witnesses who recognize the signatures of the witnesses, the document is valid, if so, anyone who wishes will forge and write and sign whatever he wishes, and collect with it! And here, R"I says that one can say [that the Gemara is referring to a case] such as where the borrower admits that he wrote it and claims that it is paid, and this tanna holds that [when] one admits regarding a document that he wrote it, [the holder] must ratify it, and this ratification is certainly by rabbinic law; alternatively, [the case is] such as where it was ratified from one field or from two fields and it emerges from his own possession, where [the Gemara] says above (Ketubot 20a) that we are concerned lest he forged [it]. However, at the beginning of Gittin (3a and there), it is proven that even where they do not recognize the signature at all, by Torah law it is as though their testimony was examined in court.

Tosafot on Ketubot 28a:15:1.hebrew: ודלמא עבד כהן הוא - פי': ועכשיו נשתחרר ונוטל שלא כדין. וקשה לרבינו יצחק: דבפ' נושאין על האנוסה (יבמות דף צט: ושם), מפרש הש"ס הא דאין חולקין תרומה לעבד — משום דלמא אתי לאסוקיה ליוחסין. מה צריך להאי טעמא? הוה ליה למימר דאין חולקין אפי' אין מעלין, שמא ישאל גם אחר שישתחרר, כדפריך הכא הש"ס! וכן מפרש התם הש"ס דאין חולקין לאשה בלא בעלה משום גרושה; ומאי טעמא נמי דמאן דאמר חולקין? וי"ל: דלא שכיחא כולי האי שישאל תרומה אחר שישתחרר, לא בתורת עבד ולא בתורת כהן, כי ירא פן יבדקוהו ויתברר שהוא עבד, ויוציאו עליו קול עבדות. ולא חיישינן נמי פן ימכרנו רבו לישראל וישאל תרומה, שהרי מזונותיו על רבו, ואין אדם חוטא ולא לו; וכולי האי לא חיישינן שמא יאמר לו רבו ישראל: "צאי מעשה ידיך במזונותיך":
Tosafot on Ketubot 28a:15:1.english: And perhaps he is the slave of a priest - Explanation: And now he has been freed and is taking [terumah] unlawfully. And it is difficult for Rabbeinu Yitzchak: For in the chapter [entitled] Nos'in Al Ha'anusah (Yevamot 99b and there), the Gemara explains that [the reason] we do not distribute terumah to a slave is because [people] might come to elevate him to [priestly] lineage. Why is this reason needed? It should have said that we do not distribute [terumah to a slave] even [according to the opinion that] we do not elevate [from terumah to lineage], lest he also request [terumah] after he is freed, just as the Gemara asks here! And similarly, the Gemara there explains that we do not distribute [terumah] to a woman without her husband because [she might be] a divorcee; and [moreover,] what is the reason of the one who says we do distribute [terumah to a slave]? And one can say: It is not so common that he would request terumah after being freed — neither in the capacity of a slave nor in the capacity of a priest — because he is afraid lest they investigate him and it become clear that he is a slave, and they spread a rumor of slavehood about him. Nor are we concerned lest his master sell him to an Israelite and he request terumah, because his sustenance is [the responsibility of] his master, and a person does not sin where there is no benefit to himself; and we are not concerned to that extent that his Israelite master might say to him, "Take your earnings for your sustenance."

Tosafot on Ketubot 28a:1:1.hebrew: ואם היה כהן לא תדור עמו במבוי - דכיון דפנויה היא קיל ליה, אבל אם נישאת אין צריך להרחיק אלא כדי שכונה, דהיינו ג' בתים, כדאמרינן בסוף פרק קמא דע"ז (דף כא.), דכיון דנישאת חמירא ליה אפי' לכהן:
Tosafot on Ketubot 28a:1:1.english: And if he was a priest, she may not live with him in an alleyway - For since she is unmarried, [the prohibition] is treated lightly by him; but if she remarried, he need only keep a distance of a neighborhood, which is three houses, as we say at the end of the first chapter of Avodah Zarah (21a), for since she has remarried, [the prohibition] is stringent for him, even for a priest.

Tosafot on Ketubot 28a:1:2.hebrew: כפר קטן נידון כשכונה - וטעמא לפי שאין בני אדם מצוין שם, ורגיל יותר לבא אצלה; ודווקא כפר קטן, אבל כפר בינוני לא:
Tosafot on Ketubot 28a:1:2.english: A small village is judged as [his immediate] proximity - And the reason is because people are not commonly found there, and he is more likely to come to her; and [this applies] specifically to a small village, but not to a medium-sized village.

Tosafot on Ketubot 28a:5:1.hebrew: רב הונא אמר נגודי מנגדינן להו - נראה לר"ת דלרב הונא נמי משמתינן וגם מנגדין, שכל אחד מחמיר מחבירו; ואם הוא אומר דנגדינן ליה בלא שמתא, הוה מיקל טפי, כדאמרינן במועד קטן (דף יז.) ובפרק מקום שנהגו (פסחים נב.): "במערבא כי מחייב צורבא מרבנן, מימנו אנגידא ולא מימנו אשמתא":
Tosafot on Ketubot 28a:5:1.english: Rav Huna said: We flog them - It appears to Rabbeinu Tam that according to Rav Huna we both excommunicate [them] and flog [them], since each one [of the Amoraim] is stricter than his colleague; whereas if he were saying that we flog him without excommunication, he would be more lenient, as we say in Moed Katan (17a) and in the chapter [entitled] Makom Shenahagu (Pesachim 52a): "In the West [the Land of Israel], when a Torah scholar incurs [a penalty], they vote for flogging, and they do not vote for excommunication."

Tosafot on Ketubot 28a:8:1.hebrew: אלו נאמנין להעיד בגודלן מה שראו בקוטנן - משמע דבקוטנן לא מהימן אפילו בדרבנן, דהא מוקי לה בגמרא בתרומה דרבנן. וקשה לריב"א, דאמר בפ"ק דפסחים (דף ד: ושם) דנאמנים על בדיקת חמץ אפי' נשים ועבדים וקטנים, ופריך: "מידי מששא אית בהו?" ומשני: הואיל ובדיקת חמץ דרבנן, הימנוהו רבנן בדרבנן. וי"ל דהתם היינו טעמא, משום דבדיקת חמץ הוא בידו, לכן נאמן אפילו קטן בדרבנן. אבל קשה, דהיכא דבידו אפי' בדאורייתא אשה מהימנא! דבפרק המדיר (לקמן כתובות דף עב. ושם) תנן: "וקוצה לה חלה", ובניקור — מעשים בכל יום שאנו סומכין עליהן. וי"ל דבירושלמי מפרש דבדיקת חמץ הוא טורח ונשים עצלניות הן, ולהכי אי לאו דבדיקת חמץ דרבנן לא הוו מהימני:
Tosafot on Ketubot 28a:8:1.english: These are deemed credible to testify in their majority [with regard to] what they saw in their minority - This implies that in their minority they are not deemed credible even with respect to a rabbinic [matter], for the Gemara establishes [the Mishnah's case of] terumah as referring to rabbinic terumah. And this is difficult for the Riva, for [a baraita] states in the first chapter of Pesachim (4b, and there [in the sugya]): Even women, slaves, and minors are deemed credible regarding the search for chametz; and [the Gemara] asks: "Is there any substance to them?" And it answers: Since searching for chametz is a rabbinic [obligation], the Rabbis deemed them credible in a rabbinic [matter]. And one can answer that there, this is the reason: because searching for chametz is within his power [to perform himself], therefore even a minor is deemed credible in a rabbinic [matter]. However, this is difficult, for wherever it is within one's power, a woman is deemed credible even in a Torah-level [matter]! For in the chapter [entitled] Hamadir (later in Ketubot 72a, and there [in the sugya]) we learned in the Mishnah: "and she sets aside challah for herself [without doing so properly]"; and regarding nikkur [removing forbidden fats and veins from meat] — it is a daily occurrence that we rely upon them. And one can answer that in the Jerusalem Talmud it explains that searching for chametz is a burden and women are lazy [about doing it], and therefore were it not that searching for chametz is a rabbinic [obligation], they would not be deemed credible.
